The Vector Local policy in effect for this Vector: on or off, Web access, the model server list, the services you allowed and what the policy files said. Also a change to your config that would loosen it and waits for you, the keys a company lock keeps, where the network log is kept, and every kind of request Vector makes.

patch.description: Change Vector Local in your user config. A change is judged by what it changes in the settings in effect, so a change your config holds is never part of it. A change that makes it stricter applies at once. One that would loosen it (turn it off, a looser Web access, a new model server, a new or removed identity pin for a server on the list, a newly allowed service or site) fails with LocalConfirmError and the list of what it loosens, unless the request says `confirm: true`, which an owner's app sends only after asking. Turning Vector Local on applies at once, and holds the services, internet model servers and sites your config lets through until you confirm them. With `held`, it applies the change your config holds instead, and only as `held` lists it. A Vector an agent started cannot loosen it, even while Vector Local is off, and under a company lock only the keys your company left to you change.

It asks for these only; it sends no prompt. With Vector Local on, only that server is let through while it is read, and Web access None keeps internet servers blocked.

200.description: The server, on the list and added as a provider

post.description: Read the server at an address, put it on the model server list with the identity it answered with, and add it to your user config as a provider with the models it runs, each with its context, reply limit, tool calling and image input. Its cloud models are left out. With Vector Local on, listing a server loosens it, so the request needs `confirm: true`, and fails with LocalConfirmError otherwise; so does adding a server on the list again when it answers as a different server, and `identity` says what changed. Headers are used to read the server and are not saved.

200.description: One row per layer, and the model check when a model was named

post.description: Read every layer of Vector Local, one row each: the switch, the policy, a held change, the network guard, unlabelled requests, Vector's own services, Web access, each model server on the list (it answers, as the server it was when added) and the network log. With `model`, it also runs that model through 2 or 3 requests with the role's real tools (agent, subagent, review for Vectorscope, judge or research) and records the result in your user config; a model the model catalog lists at a cloud address keeps the catalog's limits. It reads only servers you or your company host: never a cloud AI service, and never a server on the internet that is not on your model server list. It never loads a model too big for free memory without `confirmed`.

Let the next request of a kind Vector Local asks about through, such as a model download or a manual update check. Each grant answers one ask and is never saved. Allow a service for good with PATCH /local instead.
